title: Downy Oak: Ancient Downy Oaks You Can Visit
meta_description: Downy oak, the modest tree of Umbrian hillsides, mapped here as four exceptional specimens, including a freshly registered 30-metre giant.
intro: Downy oak is the tree Umbrian hillsides are made of, usually a modest, crooked field-edge tree that loses out to better species on good ground. The four the site maps are the exception, all in Umbria and none of them small. Two stand around Assisi: one marking the old gate onto the road to the Eremo delle Carceri, the other in the lower hamlet of Valecchie, added to Italy's national register in July 2026 as the tallest monumental tree recorded in the whole region, thirty metres up. The other two grow 150 metres apart on a lane outside Perugia, within eight centimetres of the same girth, on ground the species shares with truffles: Quercus pubescens is one of central Italy's classic truffle hosts, which is part of why a productive one gets left standing. None of the four carries a documented age; Italy's national register has never recorded one.
